surfaces.title: Jezero Crater, Mars
surfaces.creditNote: Taken by the Perseverance rover on its third day on Mars (Feb 21, 2021). The sky above and the dark ground below are filled in.
surfaces.orbitHint: Hi, I'm Orbit! Drag to look around. Then tap the glowing dots!

hotspots.label: Far away hills
hotspots.title: The edge of Jezero Crater
hotspots.text: Those far-away hills are the rim of Jezero Crater. Long ago, rivers poured into this crater and made a lake. That was more than 3.5 billion years ago!

hotspots.label: Red ground
hotspots.title: Why is Mars red?
hotspots.text: The dirt on Mars has iron in it. The iron rusts, a bit like an old bike left in the rain. That is why the ground looks red.

hotspots.label: The sky
hotspots.title: A dusty sky
hotspots.text: Mars has thin air with lots of dust floating in it. To our eyes, the sky would look hazy and red, not blue like on Earth.

hotspots.label: The rover
hotspots.title: Meet Perseverance
hotspots.text: This is Perseverance, a robot explorer on Mars. It is looking for signs of ancient life. It also collects pieces of rock to study.

hotspots.label: About this picture
hotspots.title: A picture made of 142 photos
hotspots.text: This 360 degree picture is made of 142 photos. Perseverance took them on its third day on Mars. People on Earth joined them together.
